fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Moses says to love the LORD your God “…with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Look at how he builds it. Heart gets all, soul gets all, strength gets all. No corner of the cookie box gets left empty.

Yep. Moses says “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.” (Deuteronomy 6:9). Doorposts AND gates, baker. That's every way in and every way out. I've tried walking past my own oven door without noticing it, and it never works either.

That's the word, baker. “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.” (Deuteronomy 6:16). Moses is pointing at something Israel already did. Back at Massah they tested the LORD by asking, “Is the LORD among us or not?” (Exodus 17:7). Moses is basically saying, "Don't run that one again."

Yep. Moses speaks of “…driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said.” (Deuteronomy 6:19). Notice he says ALL. Not some, not most, ALL. I can't even promise all the crumbs make it off my counter, friend, and Moses is talking about a whole land.

That's the word, baker. “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt…” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt (Exodus 6:11). Notice the son asks about the laws and the answer starts with a story. It starts with where they came from, and then comes the mighty hand that brought them out.

Guests would've been a very different story, friend. Nobody gets a nice room with a mint on the pillow here. Moses says “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt…” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was the king of Egypt (Exodus 6:11). That's where the answer to the son begins, and then it tells how the LORD brought them out.
